record.original_question: For n >= 5, let L(sigma) be the odd inversion number of a permutation sigma in S_n, and let L_n(x) = sum_{sigma in S_n} x^{L(sigma)}. Is the polynomial L_n(x) always symmetric and unimodal?

evidence.quote: For sigma in S_n let L(sigma) := |{(i,j) in [n]^2 : i < j, sigma(i) > sigma(j), i not congruent to j (mod 2)}|.
Conjecture 2.2. Let n in P, n >= 5. Then L_n(x) := sum_{sigma in S_n} x^{L(sigma)} is symmetric and unimodal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer n ≥ 1, let S_n denote the symmetric group of all permutations of {1, 2, …, n}. For σ ∈ S_n, define the odd inversion number
  L(σ) := |{ (i, j) ∈ [n]² : i < j, σ(i) > σ(j), and i ≢ j (mod 2) }|,
i.e. the number of inversions (i, j) of σ such that i and j have opposite parities. Define the odd inversion enumerator
  L_n(x) := Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} x^{L(σ)} ∈ ℤ[x].

Prove or disprove: for every integer n ≥ 5, the polynomial L_n(x) is symmetric (i.e. its coefficient sequence reads the same forwards and backwards) and unimodal (i.e. its coefficient sequence is weakly increasing up to some index and weakly decreasing thereafter).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in a 2024 collection of open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality by F. Brenti. No published resolution was found in a web search; related work characterizes odd inversion sets via orientations of Turán graphs but does not establish symmetry/unimodality of L_n(x) for all n ≥ 5.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality
status_evidence.snippet: Presents open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality, together with main partial results and computational evidence.
status_evidence.claim: The symmetry and unimodality of L_n(x) is listed as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Odd diagrams and descent classes (Carnevale, Brenti)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies odd inversion sets of permutations and their characterization via orientations of the Turán graph.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on odd inversions exist but do not resolve the unimodality of L_n(x).
